'''''Butia eriospatha''''' is a small species of ''[[Butia]]'' [[Palm (plant)|palm]] [[endemic]] to the highlands of southern Brazil.<ref name="iucn status 15 November 2021" /> It is very similar to [[Butia odorata|''B. odorata'']], but is easily distinguished from this species by the distinct spathes which are densely covered in rust-coloured, woolly hairs.<ref name=Glassman>{{cite journal |last=Glassman |first=S. F. |date=1970 |title=A conspectus of the palm genus Butia Becc. |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/19907#page/63/mode/1up |journal=Fieldiana |volume=32 |issue=10 |pages=145, 149 |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.2384 |access-date=25 September 2018|doi-access=free}}</ref> Indeed, the specific epithet is derived from Greek ''ἔριον'', wool, and Latin ''spatha'', which refers to the spathe.<ref name=Soares2015>{{cite journal |last=Soares |first=Kelen Pureza |date=2015 |title=Le genre Butia |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288181003 |language=fr |journal=Principes |volume=1 |page=25 |access-date=25 September 2018}}</ref> It has been given the name '''woolly jelly palm''' (UK) or '''wooly jelly palm''' (US) in English.<ref name=MMPND>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantnames.unimelb.edu.au/Sorting/Butia.html |title=Sorting Butia names |last=Porcher |first=Michel H. |date=20 April 2003 |website=Multilingual Multiscript Plant Name Database (MMPND) |publisher=University of Melbourne |access-date=26 September 2018}}</ref> Vernacular names for it where it is native are '''''butiá-da-serra''''',<ref name=Brazil2020>{{cite web |url=http://servicos.jbrj.gov.br/flora/search/Butia_eriospatha |title=Brazilian Flora Checklist - Butia eriospatha (Mart. ex Drude) Becc. |last1=Heiden |first1=G. |last2=Ellert-Pereira |first2=P.E. |last3=Eslabão |first3=M.P. |date=2015 |website=Butia in Lista de Espécies da Flora do Brasil, Flora do Brasil 2020 under construction |publisher=Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=CNCFlora>{{cite web |url=http://cncflora.jbrj.gov.br/portal/pt-br/profile/Butia%20eriospatha |title=Centro Nacional de Conservação da Flora - CNCFlora |last=Prieto |first=Pablo Viany |date=29 June 2012 |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=Mansfeld>{{cite web |url=http://mansfeld.ipk-gatersleben.de/apex/f?p=185:46:0::NO::module,mf_use,source,akzanz,rehm,akzname,taxid:mf,,botnam,0,,Butia+eriospatha,10973 |title=Mansfeld's World Database of Agriculture and Horticultural Crops |last=Kruse |first=J. |date=April 2001 |publisher=IPK |access-date=26 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=pollen>{{cite journal |last1=Bauermann |first1=Soraia Girardi |last2=Evaldt |first2=Andréia Cardoso Pacheco |last3=Zanchin |first3=Janaína Rosana |last4=de Loreto Bordignon |first4=Sergio Augusto |date=June 2010 |title=Diferenciação polínica de Butia, Euterpe, Geonoma, Syagrus e Thritrinax e implicações paleoecológicas de Arecaceae para o Rio Grande do Sul |url=https://isb.emnuvens.com.br/iheringia/article/view/79/86 |journal=Iheringia, Série Botânica |volume=65 |issue=1 |pages=35–46 |language=pt |issn=0073-4705 |access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref> '''''butiázeiro''''',<ref name=CNCFlora/><ref name=Mansfeld/> '''''butiá-veludo''''',<ref name=CNCFlora/> '''''butiá'''''<ref name=Glassman/><ref name=CNCFlora/> '''''butiá verdadeiro''''',<ref name=Mansfeld/> '''''butiá-do-campo''''',<ref name=Mansfeld/> '''''yatáy'''''<ref name=Mansfeld/> and '''''macumá'''''.<ref name=Glassman/><ref name=CNCFlora/>

==Taxonomy==
In 1970 Sidney Fredrick Glassman moved this species, along with all other ''Butia'', to ''[[Syagrus (plant)|Syagrus]]'',<ref name=Glassman1970>{{cite journal |last=Glassman |first=Sidney Fredrick |date=1970 |title=A conspectus of the palm genus Butia Becc. |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/19907#page/37/mode/1up |journal=Fieldiana |volume=32 |issue=10 |pages=145–149 |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.2384 |access-date=12 October 2018|doi-access=free}}</ref> but in 1979 he changed his mind and moved everything back.<ref name=Glassman1979>{{cite journal |last=Glassman |first=Sidney Fredrick |date=1979 |title=Re-evaluation of the Genus Butia With a Description of a New Species |url=http://media.e-taxonomy.eu/palmae/protologe/palm_tc_28144_P.pdf |journal=Principes |volume=23 |pages=70–71 |access-date=12 October 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
''Butia eriospatha'' is a solitary-trunked palm tree. The trunk is sometimes inclined to a side, and may occasionally be [[underground stem|subterranean]]. The 20-22 [[pinnate]] leaves arch back down towards the trunk and have a petiole armed with teeth spaced along their margins; the rachis of the leaf is 150–220 cm in length.<ref name=Brazil2020/><ref name=pollen/> The branched inflorescence develops in a woody, 115–135 cm long spathe covered in a dense woolly indumentum. The [[pistillate flower|pistillate]] (female) flowers are 5–9mm in length. The shape of the fruit is globose (round), as is the shape of the nuts.<ref name=Brazil2020/>

Like all species of ''Butia'' studied, this species has relatively larger pollen grains than that of other genera of palm present in [[Rio Grande do Sul]], Brazil. These grains are bilaterally symmetrical, prolate-spheroid, monosulcate, and with the end piriform (pear-shaped). The surface is covered in minute 2μm-large reticulate patterns.<ref name=pollen/>

==Distribution==
It is native to southern Brazil, where the main bulk of its population is found straddling the highlands in the eastern [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]]/[[Rio Grande do Sul]] border regions, surrounded by scattered sub-populations in the southeastern coastal part of the high plateau of the states of [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], Rio Grande do Sul, and Santa Catarina.<ref name=Brazil2020/><ref name=CNCFlora/> A naturalised population in an area of northern [[Misiones Province]], Argentina, was reported in 2008.<ref name=Soares2014>{{cite journal |last1=Soares |first1=Kelen Pureza |last2=Longhi |first2=Solon Jonas |last3=Neto |first3=Leopoldo Witeck |last4=de Assis |first4=Lucas Coelho |date=2014 |title=Palmeiras (Arecaceae) no Rio Grande do Sul, Brasil |url=https://rodriguesia-seer.jbrj.gov.br/index.php/rodriguesia/article/view/ID%20862/pdf_85 |language=pt |journal=Rodriguésia - Revista do Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro |volume=65 |issue=1 |page=121 |access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref>

Bauermann ''et al.'' investigated the possibility of using palm pollen, including this species, in [[palynology]], in order to try to provide more detail about the ancient changes in habitat in the state Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil by tracking the changes in distribution and abundance of the palms, but were unable to provide much detail on the subject.<ref name=pollen/>

==Habitat and ecology==
[[File:Floresta com Araucária.JPG|thumb|left|''Butia eriospatha'' in its native habitat growing with ''[[Araucaria angustifolia]]'' in the [[Tainhas State Park]].]]

It is found growing in the [[Atlantic rainforest]] [[biome]] on a plateau at higher altitudes, between 700 and 1,200m, where it is largely found in grasslands, aggregated in often extensive, dense, almost monoculture palm groves, but higher up also sometimes in open [[Araucaria moist forests|''Araucaria'' forest]].<ref name="iucn status 15 November 2021" /><ref name=Brazil2020/><ref name=Soares2014/>

These distinctive dense palm groves are known as ''butiázais'' in [[Rio Grande do Sul]],<ref name=Soares2014/> but may also be known as ''butiatuba'' or ''butiazal''.<ref name=pollen/>

The caterpillars of the butterflies [[Brassolis astyra|''Brassolis astyra'' ssp. ''astyra'']] (''fide'' d'Aralljo & Silva ''et al.'' [1968] (=record no. 2362, ''Butia eriospatha'' identified as ''butiázeiro'' or ''Cocos'' sp. in this study)) and [[Brassolis sophorae|''B. sophorae'']] (possibly ssp. ''dinizi'') (=no. 2365) have been recorded feeding on ''B. eriospatha'' in [[Santa Catarina State|Santa Catarina]]. ''[[Opsiphanes invirae]]'', the nominate form or possibly subspecies ''remoliatus'', was also recorded feeding on this palm in the same study (=no. 2390, 2392).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Penz |first1=Carla M. |last2=Aiello |first2=Annette |last3=Srygley |first3=Robert B. |date=1999 |title=Early stages of ''Caligo illioneus'' and ''C. idomeneus'' (Nymphalidae, Brassolinae) from Panama, with remarks on larval food plants for the subfamily |url=http://images.peabody.yale.edu/lepsoc/jls/1990s/1999/1999-53%284%29142-Penz.pdf |journal=Journal of the Lepidopterists' Society |volume=53 |issue=4 |pages=142–152 |access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref><ref name=funet>{{cite web |url=http://www.nic.funet.fi/pub/sci/bio/life/plants/magnoliophyta/magnoliophytina/liliopsida/arecaceae/butia/ |title=Butia |last=Savela |first=Markku |website=Lepidoptera and some other life forms |access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref>

The caterpillars of the Indonesian butterfly [[Cephrenes augiades|''Cephrenes augiades'' ssp. ''augiades'']] may also feed on the leaves this palm.<ref name=funet/>

[[File:Oviposition in Anchylorhynchus eriospathae.ogv |thumb|200px |alt=''Anchylorhynchus eriospathae'' laying its eggs in the flowers of ''Butia eriospatha''. |Video of ''Anchylorhynchus eriospathae'' laying its eggs on the developing flowers of ''Butia eriospatha''.]]

In a long term study observing the feeding behaviour throughout the year of the squirrel [[Sciurus ingrami|''Guerlinguetus brasiliensis'' ssp. ''ingrami'']] in secondary ''[[Araucaria angustifolia]]'' forest in the Parque Recreativo
Primavera in the vicinity of the city of [[Curitiba]], Paraná, of the ten plant species of which the squirrel ate the seeds or nuts, ''Butia eriospatha'' was an uncommon but regular part of the diet in the spring and summer. Mushrooms, seeds of ''Araucaria angustifolia'', nuts of ''[[Syagrus romanzoffiana]]'' (queen palm) and acorns of ''[[Quercus robur]]'' (English oak) were the main part of the diet depending on the season.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bordignon |first1=Marcelo |last2=Monteiro-Filho |first2=E. L. A. |date=1999 |title=Seasonal Food Resources of the Squirrel ''Sciurus ingrami'' in a Secondary ''Araucaria'' Forest in Southern Brazil |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233029598 |journal=Studies on Neotropical Fauna and Environment |volume=34 |issue=3 |pages=137–140 |doi=10.1076/snfe.34.3.137.8910 |access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref>

==Uses==
''Butia eriospatha'' is reasonably available in Europe as an ornamental. It is often used in mild temperate climates as a [[hardy palms|hardy palm]] for its exotic look.

Products obtained from the palm are used locally and are not widely marketed.<ref name=CNCFlora/> The fruit pulp is used as a base to make beverages.<ref name=Mansfeld/><ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=2018-09-26}}</ref> A wine is made from the palm, as are juices and jellies/jams.<ref name=CNCFlora/>

Fibres were once harvested from this palm,<ref name=Mansfeld/> which were used to make mattresses. Plantations of this palm were planted in the 1950s in Brazil for this purpose.

===Horticulture===
It is sometimes cultivated in Brazil and Argentina.<ref name=Mansfeld/>

It is advised to plant the palms in full sunlight. It is said to take −14 °C, but should be protected at −6 °C in [[the Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eawagelaar.nl/Butia.html |title=Het geslacht Butia |last=Wagelaar |first=Edwin |date=31 December 2017 |website=Palmexotica |language=nl |access-date=3 October 2018}}</ref>

==Conservation==
The species is widely cultivated, but according to Noblick in 1998, wild populations are declining.<ref name="iucn status 15 November 2021" /> It was listed as ''em perigo'' (endangered) by the Rio Grande do Sul state government in 2002 (''decreto'' nº 42.099) and 2014 (''decreto'' n° 52.109), because the population is believed to have been reduced by over 50% in at least the last 100 years.<ref name=Soares2014/><ref>{{cite act |title=Decreto n° 52.109/2014 |trans-title= |type= |number= |language=Portuguese |date=2014 |article=52.109 |article-type=Decreto |page= |url=http://www.fzb.rs.gov.br/upload/20141222112707decreto52109_2014_flora.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://secweb.procergs.com.br/livlof/?id_modulo=2&id_uf=23&ano=2013 |title=Lista das Espécies Ameaçadas de Extinção no RS |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Avaliação do Estado de Conservação de Espécies Flora - RS - 2014 |publisher=FZB RS - Fundação Zoobotânica do Rio Grande do Sul |language=pt |access-date=25 September 2018}}</ref>

In 2012 the [[Centro Nacional de Conservação da Flora]] rated the conservation status for Brazil as 'vulnerable'.<ref name=CNCFlora/>
